newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Telecom plans int'l service next spring.
newsitem.headline: Japan Telecom plans int'l service next spring.

text.p: Japan Telecom Co plans to launch international telecommunications services in the spring of 1998 by connecting its lines with those of Japanese international carriers, a company official said on Tuesday.

Long-distance carrier Japan Telecom is talking with three international carriers -- Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd, IDC Corp and ITJ Inc -- about conditions for using each other's phone lines, Japan Telecom director Taro Sasaki told a news conference.
Japan Telecom also plans to start an international service using communications satellite Asiasat 2 next spring, initially to four or five Asian countries, he said.
Tariffs and other conditions for leasing Asiasat's circuits from Singapore's Hutchison Corporate Access have not yet been decided, he said.
Japan Telecom and Hutchison Corporate Access, a unit of the Hutchison Whampoa Ltd group, signed a preliminary agreement on the use of Asiasat's circuits on Monday, Sasaki said.
Sasaki said profitability in the international communications business would be low, but added:
"We need to provide our customers with seamless communications services, including local and international calls, or we will lose in competition."
Capital expenditure, sales targets and other details for the planned international business have not yet been decided, he said.
